newsitem.title: UK: British widow can have sperm treatment abroad - court.
newsitem.headline: British widow can have sperm treatment abroad - court.

text.p: A British widow on Thursday won a court battle to try to have a baby using her dead husband's frozen sperm, but only abroad.

Three Court of Appeal judges ruled that the authority which governs artificial fertilisation was right to refuse Diane Blood permission to have the treatment in Britain but said the insemination could go ahead in Belgium.

"The authority's decision was correct that treatment in the UK could not take place without Mr Blood's consent. The authority was not properly advised as to the importance of EC (European) law as to treatment in Belgium," the judgment said.
"She has the right to be treated in Belgium with her husband's sperm unless there are good public policy reasons for not allowing this to happen."
The Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority had banned Blood from using her late husband Stephen's frozen sperm because she did not have his written permission.
Blood says the sperm sample was taken from her husband when he was still alive and written consent should not have been necessary.
